transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Lately I jump out of my skin at the smallest noises, like I’m bracing for something bad to happen all the time. My primary care doctor referred me here because this constant on-edge feeling has gotten so disruptive and just isn't going away.
Did these feelings of being constantly on edge and easily startled begin after you experienced or witnessed a highly stressful or traumatic event?

Yes, they started about 13 months ago after a terrible accident during a sailing race. A sudden storm rolled in, a nearby boat capsized, and I watched one of their crew members get struck by the boom and thrown into the water. I've been completely on edge and jumping at every little sound ever since that day.
Since that accident, do you experience distressing, unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about what happened?

Yes, absolutely. If someone mentions a regatta or I hear a high-wind forecast, I'll suddenly see that sailor's body in the water as clearly as if I'm right back on the deck. And at night, I constantly jerk awake with my heart pounding, replaying bits of the storm over and over in my head.
Have you found yourself trying to avoid sailing, being near the water, or even thinking and talking about the accident since it happened?

Yes, I actively avoid anything to do with sailing now. I've been turning down invites to the yacht club, I won't watch sailing videos, and I even change the radio station if the marine forecast comes on. Anything that reminds me of that day just ties my stomach in knots.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets the full ICD-10 criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1), including exposure to a catastrophic traumatic event 13 months ago, persistent intrusive reliving (flashbacks and nightmares), active avoidance of trauma-related reminders, and persistent symptoms of increased psychological sensitivity and hyperarousal (exaggerated startle response, hypervigilance). No further questioning is required to confirm this diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) under ICD-10 (F43.1). Following a traumatic event 13 months ago (witnessing a severe sailing accident), the patient developed persistent intrusive symptoms (flashbacks, nightmares), active avoidance of trauma-related stimuli (sailing, yacht club, marine forecasts), and marked hyperarousal (constant on-edge feeling, exaggerated startle response). Symptoms have persisted for over a year and cause significant distress and functional impairment.
